THE PLAYBOOK
Hospitality Standard — All Venues款待服務準則——全體分店
Core Vision核心願景
Hospitality first, not just SOPs.
  • Simple, memorable, easy to spot in action
  • Same rules for every role, every seniority
  • Every team member meets a guest at some point — so it applies to all of us
款待為先，不只是SOP。
  • 簡單、好記、容易被看見
  • 不分職位與資歷，人人適用
  • 每位同仁都會遇到顧客——所以這適用於我們每一個人
The Playbook — 9 BehaviorsThe Playbook——9項行為準則
1
Safety First, Always安全至上，永遠優先
  • Safety outranks friendliness, speed, and sales. No interaction matters if someone gets hurt.安全的重要性高於親切、效率與業績。若有人因此受傷，再好的互動都毫無意義。
  • Recognize signs of intoxication, distress, or conflict early, and act — never wait to be told.及早察覺醉態、情緒困擾或衝突跡象，主動處理——不要等別人告訴你。
  • Know your escalation path: when to loop in a manager or security, and do it without hesitation or embarrassment.清楚知道你的升報流程：何時該通知主管或安全人員，並且毫不猶豫、不覺得尷尬地去做。
  • There is no safety call that is "someone else's job."沒有任何安全狀況是「別人的事」。
✓ Good: A server flags a visibly over-served guest to a manager immediately, before it becomes a problem.✓ 好的示範：服務生在顧客明顯喝多之前，立刻回報主管，防患於未然。
✗ Miss: Staff notice a guest in distress or a brewing conflict and hope someone else handles it.✗ 疏失示範：同仁注意到顧客情緒不穩或衝突正在醞釀，卻期待別人來處理。
2
Hospitality Begins With Each Other款待，從彼此開始
  • Every team member acknowledges and greets fellow team members when entering the venue.每位同仁進入場館時，都要主動招呼並問候其他同仁。
  • The hospitality we give our guests starts with how we treat each other.我們給予顧客的款待，從我們彼此對待的方式開始。
  • Guests should never see staff conflict, frustration, or venting — settle it off the floor, never in front of the room.顧客絕不應看見同仁間的衝突、不耐或情緒發洩——有問題到內場解決，絕不在顧客面前。
  • What happens at a table stays at the table. Guest privacy and confidentiality are part of how we care for people.桌邊發生的事，留在桌邊。顧客隱私與保密，是我們照顧他人的一部分。
✓ Good: Greeting a coworker by name when you walk in, even mid-rush; taking a disagreement into the back instead of the floor.✓ 好的示範：即使在尖峰時段，進場時仍以名字問候同事；有意見不合就到內場解決，而非在外場。
✗ Miss: Walking past a teammate without acknowledgment, or airing frustration with a coworker in front of guests.✗ 疏失示範：走過同事身邊卻毫無回應，或在顧客面前發洩對同事的不滿。
3
The 3 × 3 Rule3×3法則
  • Within 3 meters / 3 seconds, acknowledge anyone who crosses your path — guest or teammate.在3公尺內、3秒內，向任何與你交會的人打招呼——無論是顧客或同仁。
  • Eye contact, smile, and a genuine greeting.眼神交流、微笑，發自內心的問候。
  • Use their name whenever you know it.只要知道對方名字，就直接稱呼。
  • Never allow a guest — or a coworker — to feel invisible in our space.絕不讓顧客——或同事——在我們的場館裡感覺自己被忽視。
✓ Good: A cook in the hallway makes eye contact and greets a guest by name walking to the restroom.✓ 好的示範：廚師在走道上與前往洗手間的顧客眼神交流，並以名字問候。
✗ Miss: Staff look down or turn away as a guest passes within arm's reach.✗ 疏失示範：顧客近在咫尺經過時，同仁卻低頭或轉身迴避。
4
See It Before They Ask在對方開口前先察覺
  • Notice the empty glass, the searching look, the guest patting their pockets for a card — before they have to ask.留意空了的酒杯、四處張望的眼神、顧客摸口袋找卡片的動作——在他們開口之前就先察覺。
  • Anticipation is what makes hospitality feel effortless instead of transactional.預先設想需求，才能讓款待顯得自然而不像單純的交易。
  • If you're not sure what someone needs, approach and ask — don't wait for them to flag you down.若不確定對方需要什麼，主動上前詢問——不要等對方招手才行動。
✓ Good: A server refills water or clears a plate before it's requested.✓ 好的示範：服務生在顧客開口前，主動補水或收走空盤。
✗ Miss: A guest has to visibly search for staff to get something they clearly need.✗ 疏失示範：顧客明顯需要協助，卻得四處張望尋找同仁。
5
Own It, Don't Outsource It承擔到底，不要轉手
  • If someone needs directions, take them there yourself — don't point across the room.若有人需要指引方向，親自帶對方過去——不要只是用手指方向。
  • If someone has a problem, it's yours until it's solved or you've personally handed it to someone who can solve it.若有人遇到問題，這個問題就是你的，直到解決，或你已親自將其交接給能解決的人為止。
  • There is no "that's not my job" and walking away. You stay until the handoff is complete.沒有「這不是我的工作」然後轉身走開這回事。你必須留到交接完成為止。
  • This applies to teammates too — a coworker who's lost, overwhelmed, or stuck gets the same treatment.這也適用於同仁——迷路、不知所措或卡住的同事，也應獲得同樣的對待。
✓ Good: A dishwasher notices a guest looking for the exit and walks them to the door instead of pointing.✓ 好的示範：洗碗同仁注意到顧客在找出口，親自帶對方走到門口，而非只是指方向。
✗ Miss: Pointing a guest "that way" and turning back to your task without checking they made it.✗ 疏失示範：隨手一指說「那邊」，就轉身回去做自己的事，也不確認對方是否順利找到。
6
Always Offer a Solution永遠提供解決方案
  • Don't stop at "No," "We can't," or "That's not possible."不要只停在「不行」、「我們沒辦法」或「這不可能」。
  • Explain what is possible and offer the best available alternative.說明可行的做法，並提供當下最好的替代方案。
  • We don't promise what we cannot deliver — but we always try to find a way forward.我們不承諾做不到的事——但我們永遠努力找出可行的方法。
✓ Good: "We're out of that dish, but the chef recommends this instead — can I bring it out for you?"✓ 好的示範：「這道菜目前售完，不過主廚推薦這道——我可以為您上這道嗎？」
✗ Miss: "Sorry, we don't have that" with no follow-up offered.✗ 疏失示範：只說「抱歉，我們沒有這個」，卻沒有提供任何替代方案。
7
Thank Every Guest感謝每一位顧客
  • Every departing guest should be acknowledged whenever reasonably possible.只要合理可行，每一位離場的顧客都應獲得回應與致意。
  • Thank them genuinely, using their name whenever you know it, and invite them back.真誠地道謝，只要知道名字就直接稱呼，並邀請對方再次光臨。
  • The final interaction matters just as much as the first.最後一刻的互動，與第一刻同樣重要。
✓ Good: Making eye contact and thanking a guest by the door, even during a busy close.✓ 好的示範：即使收店正忙碌，仍在門口與顧客眼神交流並致謝。
✗ Miss: Letting guests leave unacknowledged because everyone's focused on closing tasks.✗ 疏失示範：因為大家都忙著收店工作，讓顧客默默離開卻無人回應。
8
Check on Each Other彼此照應
  • If a teammate is overwhelmed and you have capacity, step in without waiting to be asked.若同事忙不過來，而你還有餘力，主動支援，不必等對方開口。
  • Protect the team.保護你的團隊。
  • Great hospitality is a team sport.卓越的款待，是一場團隊合作的競賽。
✓ Good: Jumping on a table run for a slammed teammate without being asked.✓ 好的示範：主動幫手忙腳亂的同事跑桌，不需對方開口要求。
✗ Miss: Standing idle while a coworker is visibly buried, waiting to be asked for help.✗ 疏失示範：明明同事忙得不可開交，自己卻站著等對方開口求助。
9
Leave It Better Than You Found It讓一切比你接手時更好
  • Don't walk past something that needs attention.不要對需要處理的事視而不見、逕自走過。
  • Reset, straighten, replenish, clean, communicate, and prepare.歸位、整理、補充、清潔、溝通、準備。
  • Leave your station, section, venue, and team better than you found them.讓你的崗位、區域、場館與團隊，都比你接手時更好。
✓ Good: Wiping down a station or restocking napkins on your way past, unprompted.✓ 好的示範：經過崗位時，主動擦拭檯面或補充餐巾，無需被交代。
✗ Miss: Walking past a mess or an empty station and leaving it for the next shift.✗ 疏失示範：看到雜亂或空缺的崗位卻視而不見，留給下一班處理。
The Operating Philosophy營運哲學
We don't just serve food and drinks. We create experiences people choose to come back to. 我們提供的不只是餐點與飲品，而是讓人願意一再回訪的體驗。
Service vs. Hospitality服務 vs. 款待
Service is getting the order right — the drink arrives, the table is bussed, the bill is correct. Hospitality is how getting it right makes someone feel. The Playbook exists to build hospitality, not just service; service is the baseline, hospitality is the standard. 服務，是把事情做對——飲品送達、桌面清理乾淨、帳單無誤。款待，則是把事情做對之後，讓對方產生的感受。The Playbook的存在，是為了打造款待，而不只是服務；服務是基本門檻，款待才是我們的標準。
How We Prioritize Our People我們如何排列優先順序
Care starts on the inside. If our own team doesn't feel looked after, there's no version of us that can make a guest feel that way either — you can't pour from an empty cup. So we're deliberate about the order things flow in: 關懷從內部開始。如果我們自己的團隊都感受不到被照顧，我們就不可能讓顧客感受到那樣的關懷——你不能從空杯子裡倒出東西。所以，我們刻意安排了關懷流動的順序：
  • Our team first. People who feel respected and backed by us are the only people who can genuinely make someone else feel welcome.我們的團隊，第一順位。感受到被尊重與支持的人，才有能力讓別人也感受到真正的歡迎。
  • Our guests next. Not served by a team running on fumes, but by one that's already been taken care of.我們的顧客，第二順位。不是由疲於奔命的團隊服務，而是由已經被照顧好的團隊服務。
  • The neighborhoods we're part of. Every venue exists inside a community, not apart from it.我們所屬的社區，第三順位。每間場館都存在於一個社區之中，而非置身事外。
  • The people we work with outside our walls. Suppliers and partners are collaborators in this, not just line items.牆外與我們合作的人們，第四順位。供應商與合作夥伴是共同參與者，而不只是帳目上的一筆項目。
  • The business, last. Get the first four right and the numbers take care of themselves — not the other way around.事業本身，最後一位。把前四項做對，數字自然會跟上——而不是反過來。
None of this is a ranking of who matters — everyone here matters. It's an order of operations: take care of the people closest to the work, and everything past that gets easier. It also tells you who we hire. You can teach someone to pour, to plate, to run a POS system, in a week. You can't as easily teach someone to actually care. We look for that instinct first and build the skill on top of it. 這並不是在排列誰比較重要——這裡的每一個人都很重要。這是一種執行順序：先照顧離工作現場最近的人，之後的一切都會愈來愈順暢。這也決定了我們用人的標準。倒酒、擺盤、操作POS系統，這些一週內就能教會。但真正懂得關心他人，卻沒那麼容易教。我們優先尋找這種本能，再於其上培養技藝。
Manager's Pre-Shift Guide主管開班會指南
Use this during daily pre-shift to keep The Playbook alive — not read verbatim, just as a 2-minute anchor. Default to the rotation order below, one rule per shift, cycling continuously. Break the rotation any day something notable just happened on the floor (a great save or a clear miss) — cover that rule instead, then resume the sequence where you left off. 每日開班會時使用，讓The Playbook持續發揮作用——不需要逐字朗讀，只需作為一個2分鐘的提醒錨點。預設依下列輪替順序，每班次一條準則，持續循環。若當天外場發生了值得一提的事(一次漂亮的補救，或一次明顯的疏失)，可以中斷輪替順序，改為講解該準則，之後再從中斷處繼續原本的順序。
Pre-Shift Routine (2 minutes)開班會流程（2分鐘）
  • Name today's rule and read its core line.說出今天的準則，並唸出其核心重點。
  • Give one real example from a recent shift — a win or a miss, no names needed unless it's a direct coaching moment.舉一個近期班次的真實案例——無論是成功或疏失，除非是直接指導的時刻，否則不需要指名道姓。
  • Ask one team member to share their own example or how they'd apply it today.邀請一位同仁分享自己的案例，或今天會如何應用這條準則。
Rotation Reference輪替參考
Cycles through Rules 1–9 in order, repeating continuously.依序循環準則1至9，週而復始。
The Accountability Ladder問責天梯
This is how The Playbook moves from a poster on the wall to a standard staff are actually held to. 這是The Playbook從牆上的一張海報，變成同仁實際被要求遵守的標準的方式。
1. In-the-Moment Coaching (first miss)當下指導（第一次疏失）
A private, immediate, non-written correction, same day: "Hey, that was a Rule [#] moment — here's what it should've looked like." This is coaching, not discipline. 私下、立即、當天進行、不需書面紀錄的糾正：「嘿，剛剛那個情況是第[#]條準則的時刻——正確的做法應該是這樣。」這是指導，不是懲處。
2. Logged Miss (repeated or serious)記錄疏失（重複或嚴重）
A repeated miss of the same rule, or one serious miss (e.g. ignoring a guest complaint outright), gets logged: date, rule number, what happened. One line is enough — the point is visibility over time, not paperwork. 同一條準則重複疏失，或單一次嚴重疏失（例如完全忽視顧客投訴），需被記錄：日期、準則編號、發生的事。一行文字就足夠——重點在於長期的可視性，而不是書面作業。
3. Formal Conversation (pattern)正式面談（形成模式）
Three logged misses across any rules within a 60-day window triggers a formal, documented conversation. This gives a concrete pattern to point to instead of a vague impression. 60天內，任何準則累積達3次記錄疏失，即觸發正式、書面記錄的面談。這能提供具體的模式依據，而非模糊的印象。
4. Recognition (the other side of the ladder)表揚（天梯的另一面）
Log standout moments against a rule number too, the same lightweight way. This is what feeds recognition, reviews, and eventually shows who is actually living The Playbook — not just avoiding misses. 以同樣輕量的方式，記錄同仁在某條準則上的傑出表現。這將作為表揚、績效考核的依據，最終顯示出誰是真正實踐The Playbook的人——而不只是沒有犯錯而已。

RSF-OPS-001A
Daily Opening Checklist — MOD FOH
Key Standards
  • Arrive 90 min before opening
  • Conduct full venue walkthrough — FOH, bar, restrooms
  • Verify POS, tablets, and reservation system are live
  • Run T-30 staff briefing covering specials, 86 list, VIPs
  • Sign off Opening Checklist at T-5, then open doors
